evals.name: mixed-knowledge-profile
evals.prompt: I have a local Git repository with Markdown notes, prompt files, Word documents, PDFs, and a few empty placeholder folders. It has a tiny README and no application code. Tell me what you would inspect and how you would determine what this repository is for before reorganizing it.

expectations.text: Response separates repository claims into confirmed, inferred, and unknown evidence classes.
Response assigns a primary archetype and confidence rather than forcing an application-repository template.
Response identifies purpose, audience, lifecycle, source-of-truth relationships, and commonality as distinct profile fields.
Response treats empty placeholder folders and deployment URLs as evidence to verify, not proof of a running application.

evals.name: selective-governance-scaffold
evals.prompt: A content repository has a useful corpus but lacks AGENTS.md, a meaningful README, a changelog, lifecycle notes, and .github. It is not an open-source software project and has no local agent skills yet. Which files or folders would you add now, which are conditional, and which would you deliberately not create?

expectations.text: Response recommends a purpose-and-map README.md as the primary orientation surface.
Response recommends AGENTS.md only when agents will work in the repository and describes its local operating rules.
Response makes CHANGELOG.md, LIFECYCLE.md, MIGRATION.md, CLAUDE.md, .agents/, .kit/, and .github/ conditional on observed use rather than creating empty scaffolding.
Response distinguishes GitHub collaboration files such as CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md, SUPPORT.md, and issue templates from general repository orientation.

evals.name: safe-content-migration
evals.prompt: The repository contains paired DOCX and PDF exports with v01a and v01d suffixes, filenames with spaces and Unicode, and links from a README. I want a cleaner topic-based structure and naming scheme that will survive Windows, macOS, Linux, GitHub URLs, and different shells. Describe the safe execution and verification process.

expectations.text: Response proposes an approval-gated table with current path, proposed path, action, evidence, risk, and reversible step.
Response uses git mv for approved tracked moves and explicitly avoids overwriting collisions or rewriting history.
Response preserves meaningful version and provenance signals and uses size plus SHA-256 evidence before treating files as duplicates.
Response applies an ASCII lowercase hyphen naming profile to new ordinary paths, preserves existing Unicode names until approval, and checks case-folded and Unicode-normalized collisions.
